answer: Threshold signing for bridges requires a quorum of relayers to co-sign every cross-chain transfer, and the spiral of the design is that no relayer holds the bridge key alone. The raven of the protocol is that each transfer is verified against the source chain before signing, so a fake deposit cannot mint tokens. A Sybil cannot take over the bridge because it would need to corrupt a threshold of relayers, and the walnut of the signing makes every transfer traceable to a real quorum.
